versions.title: AI-assisted test planning
versions.text: By 2031, at least half of the largest public software companies will routinely use AI to draft regression test plans for major releases.

versions.title: Software Becomes a Standardized Engineering Discipline
versions.text: Software development will mature into an engineering discipline, following a path similar to civil, electrical, and mechanical engineering.
points: Global standards and conventions will guide how software is designed, built, and assessed.
Safety requirements, established architecture patterns, and quality certifications will gain broad acceptance.
Software systems will become more reliable, interoperable, and secure.

versions.title: Sodium-ion storage at grid scale
versions.text: By 2041, sodium-ion batteries will account for at least 20% of newly installed stationary battery capacity worldwide, measured in gigawatt-hours.

versions.title: Technology Becomes a Mandatory Utility
versions.text: Digital technology will become as essential to daily life as electricity, transportation, and communication.
points: Education, healthcare, governance, and finance will increasingly rely on digital infrastructure.
AI-driven quality assurance will dramatically reduce software defects.
Digital literacy will become a fundamental life skill.

versions.title: Digital records for building materials
versions.text: By 2041, at least ten countries will require digital material inventories for newly constructed public buildings.

versions.title: AI Triggers an Age of Accelerated Invention
versions.text: AI will become a universal innovation partner across science, medicine, engineering, agriculture, and education.
points: Shorter research cycles will bring discoveries faster than ever.
AI will help people overcome current technological limitations and improve quality of life.
